subject: Aurelia Health Systems: private footprint activation checklist & egress gating
messages:
From: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@aureliahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: network-team@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: New private deployment — high-level ask and egress constraints

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. We are ready to start scoping a private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge) for our imaging inference workloads. Before we book a kickoff we need a short checklist from Redwood that outlines the networking & egress prerequisites your team requires so we can validate with our network/security teams.

Specific asks we have up front:
- Minimum required outbound egress ports/IPs for control plane and telemetry.
- KMS/HSM integration options and expected PKI requirements.
- Whether we need a public NAT gateway for model downloads or if a private mirror is supported.
- Any IP allowlist artifacts we should provision in our firewall.

Can you please send a concise preflight checklist and an initial set of artifacts we can share with our infra team? Attaching our very small network inventory for context (will send official spreadsheet after).

Thanks,
Sara Mendoza
Head of Platform Ops
Aurelia Health Systems

Attachment: aurelia_network_inventory_summary.txt (stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: New private deployment — high-level ask and egress constraints

Sara —

Thanks — this is great context. I put together a short preflight checklist below to make validation with your security/networking team straightforward. I also attached a YAML VPC template and a statement of work draft to accelerate scheduling.

Redwood private deployment preflight (high level):
1) Network & egress
   - Outbound HTTPS (443) to the Redwood control plane endpoints: 52.23.16.0/24 and 34.210.189.0/24 (preferred to allow FQDNs rdw-infer-control.redwood.com).
   - Optional outbound 443 to model artifact mirrors if you prefer private pulls: allow the S3 endpoint or provide a private NFS mirror.
   - Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) for resolution to our FQDNs or consume internal DNS forwarding entries.
   - TCP ephemeral for KV/cache traffic (recommended to be allowed within your VPC CIDR for edge nodes).
2) Identity & keys
   - KMS integrations supported: AWS KMS (grant access via ARN), HashiCorp Vault (token policy), or customer HSM (NIST 800-2x compatible).
   - We will provide a public key for verifying signed artifacts; private key stays with you.
3) Service accounts & firewall artifacts
   - Provide at least one service account with role binding for deployment tasks; we will list minimal IAM permissions in the onboarding doc.
   - Provide CIDR ranges for any egress middleboxes you want us to use for telemetry hops.
4) Ops and telemetry
   - Outbound to our metrics/trace collector endpoints (443) — can be routed via a VPC endpoint or allowed directly.
   - If you restrict outbound, we can send batched telemetry through an SFTP/HTTPS relay.
5) Deployment & downloads
   - Model downloads can be pulled via HTTPS from our artifact mirrors. If you require air-gapped installs, we provide an on-prem bundle (requires offline approval).
   - Confirm whether artifact-origin checks are possible on your side (SHA256 verification).
Next steps: if this list looks good, can you confirm your egress policy (FQDN allow vs IP allow) and the preferred KMS option? Once we have that Ben will propose a one-week tech kickoff and Karthik will run a quick network smoke test plan.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurelia_vpc_template.yaml, redwood_onboard_sow_v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: New private deployment — high-level ask and egress constraints

Eve / Karthik —

Forwarding Sara's note. Two quick internal items before we send anything to legal/security:
- Confirm the control plane FQDNs are ok to share (I used placeholder IP ranges above). If we can depend on FQDNs only, that's preferable from their side.
- Karthik: can you draft a minimal list of port checks we should run from Aurelia's staging VPC during the smoke run? Keep it to fail-fast checks (443, DNS, NTP).

I'll slot this into next Tuesday for the kickoff unless we hear otherwise.

—Ben
Lead Onboarding Engineer

From: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@aureliahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: network-team@aureliahealth.com, ops@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-11T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: New private deployment — high-level ask and egress constraints

Evelyn, Ben —

Thanks for the checklist. Our security team prefers allowlisting FQDNs & managed certificates rather than raw IPs where possible. A few clarifications from our side:
- We will not permit inbound public IPs to edge nodes; all outbound only and NATed from our egress layer.
- We need to confirm if Redwood can support placement behind our corporate proxy for control plane calls (we use an authenticated TLS proxy).
- For KMS we are leaning toward Vault; please send the expected policy scopes and token exchange pattern.

Attached is our formal egress spreadsheet and a short network diagram. Can you confirm whether the model artifact mirror can be hosted in our S3 with signed URLs (preferred) and whether that changes the deployment flow?

Cheers,
Sara

Attachments: aurelia-egress-requirements.xlsx, aurelia-network-diagram.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: New private deployment — high-level ask and egress constraints

Sara —

Short answers and next steps from our networking team: 
- FQDN allowlist: yes, we can operate with FQDNs and support certificate pinning/managed certs. We will provide the canonical FQDNs and SHA256 of the cert used by control plane endpoints ahead of the kickoff.
- Corporate proxy support: supported. We'll run a quick proxy connectivity validation during the smoke test; please provide an authenticated test endpoint or temporary proxy credential (secure token).
- Model artifacts: hosting artifacts in your S3 with signed URLs is supported and will reduce egress surface. We will still perform SHA256 verification on every artifact before install.

Planned smoke-run checklist (fail-fast):
1) DNS resolution for rdw-infer-control.redwood.com
2) Outbound TLS to control plane FQDN (443) + cert validation (presented cert SHA256 match)
3) Signed artifact download from customer S3 using a presigned URL (small 10MB sample)
4) KMS handshake: validate Vault token exchange and minimum scope access
5) Telemetry: attempt TLS handshake to metrics endpoint (443) — if blocked, switch to batched SFTP relay.

Grace (ops): we'll need a short runbook for how we will collect packet captures and logs during the smoke run for troubleshooting. Ben — can you prepare the runbook template and the temporary test artifacts?

I'll follow up with a concise checklist doc and an action item list for the kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Networking Lead — Redwood Inference
